concepts.label: test-driven development
concepts.definition: Developing by first writing an automated test that fails, then making it pass, then refactoring the code while keeping behavior working.

concepts.label: refactoring
concepts.definition: Changing software's internal structure to make it easier to understand or cheaper to modify without changing its observable behavior.

concepts.label: design by contract
concepts.definition: Specifying explicit caller preconditions, routine postconditions and state invariants as responsibilities between software elements.

references.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
references.locator: Pragmatic Paranoia, Topic 23, Design by Contract and Implementing DBC

concepts.label: mutation testing
concepts.definition: Assessing tests by deliberately changing production code and checking whether the tests detect those changes.

concepts.label: ubiquitous language
concepts.definition: A shared, precise domain-model language used by developers and domain experts.

concepts.label: property-based testing
concepts.definition: Testing general properties over generated input domains and seeking counterexamples when a property fails.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests an automated failing test first, implementation sufficient to pass it, then refactoring before the next case.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No failing-test-first, pass, then refactor cycle is requested. Tests after implementation, rerunning tests, or test additions alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is test-driven development.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests changes to software's internal code structure to improve readability, design or duplication while preserving observable behavior, including actual renaming of code elements.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No behavior-preserving internal code change is requested. Adding behavior, fixing user-visible behavior, changing external contracts, or documentation-only naming conventions alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is refactoring.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests explicit caller preconditions, routine postconditions and persistent state invariants or responsibilities between software elements.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No explicit caller preconditions, routine postconditions and state invariants or responsibilities are requested. Ordinary input validation, schema compatibility, or an isolated assertion alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is design by contract.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests deliberate changes to production code to assess whether tests detect the changed behavior.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No deliberate production-code changes to assess test detection are requested. Implementation edits, changing test inputs, fuzzing, or coverage measurement alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is mutation testing.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests that developers and domain experts use a shared precise vocabulary for the domain model.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No shared precise domain-model vocabulary for developers and domain experts is requested. Naming conventions, technical abbreviations, or an unrelated glossary alone do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is ubiquitous language.

recognition.matches: `prompt` requests testing general correctness properties over generated inputs from a domain.
recognition.doesNotMatch: No tests of general correctness properties over generated inputs are requested. Hand-picked examples only, random performance runs without correctness properties, or production-code mutation alone without generated-property tests do not match.
recognition.tip: A term for this activity is property-based testing.
